unmapped_findings: Fe-30Mn-1.2C-4Al is an intermediate Al variant: alloys with 4 wt.% and 6 wt.% Al are only very weakly affected by the applied aging treatments (450/500/550/600 °C, 0/1/24 h) in terms of mechanical data, compared with Fe-30Mn-1.2C (weakening/embrittlement) and Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al (strengthening).

For the intermediate Al variants with 2–6 wt.% Al (including 4Al), a much smaller influence of aging on tensile behavior is observed; pronounced strengthening during aging is attributed mainly to nm-sized κ-carbides in the ~8 wt.% Al variant.

For Al content below 5 wt.%, a single austenite phase prevails at room temperature; for 25–30 wt.% Mn with up to 4–5 wt.% Al (when naturally aged) the TWIP effect prevails as the deformation mechanism (SIMPLEX steels).

κ-carbides (L′1₂ structure, approximate stoichiometry (Fe,Mn)₃AlC) have a lattice mismatch below 3% with respect to an austenitic Fe-Mn-C matrix and can form cuboidal nanoprecipitates; they are thermally very stable at 600 °C and prevail after 100 h heat treatment with only modest coarsening (general κ-carbide statements, not specifically quantified for the 4Al sample).
